// Catalogue of the UK money tools in this repository and a deterministic
// matcher from "what applies to me" to "which tool answers it". No network.

  ["over100k", "I earn over £100,000"],
  ["children", "I get Child Benefit"],
  ["married", "I'm married or in a civil partnership"],
  ["selfemployed", "I'm self-employed or a sole trader"],
  ["sidehustle", "I have side income or sell things"],
  ["company", "I run (or am thinking of) a limited company"],
  ["contractor", "I'm a contractor (IR35)"],
  ["construction", "I'm a subcontractor in construction (CIS)"],

  ["Employing people", "uk-unfair-dismissal-compensation-calculator", "UK unfair dismissal compensation calculator", "Estimate the basic and compensatory award for an unfair dismissal claim, the cap, and the three-months-less-a-day deadline.", ["leave", "employed"]],
];

export const SAMPLE = { picked: ["selfemployed", "landlord"] };

export function match(picked) {
  const set = new Set(picked || []);
  const out = [];
  for (const [category, slug, title, job, tags] of TOOLS) {
    const hits = tags.filter((t) => set.has(t));
    if (hits.length) out.push({ category, slug, title, job, hits, score: hits.length });
  }
  out.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score || a.title.localeCompare(b.title));
  return out;
}

export function categories() {
  const seen = [];
  for (const t of TOOLS) if (!seen.includes(t[0])) seen.push(t[0]);
  return seen.map((c) => ({ name: c, tools: TOOLS.filter((t) => t[0] === c) }));
}

export function summaryText(rows) {
  if (!rows.length) return "No tools matched. Tick at least one situation.";
  return rows.map((r, i) => `${i + 1}. ${r.title} - ${r.job}\n   ../${r.slug}/`).join("\n");
}

What it does, and what it leaves to you

    
    
      
  • Covers: pointing you at the right calculator for your situation from the 53 UK tools in this collection.
    • 
      
  • Gives: a ranked list with a one-line description and a link for each tool.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: whether a rule applies to your exact facts, which tax year is right for you, or anything that changed after the tools were written. Each calculator lists what it does not model.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Common questions

    
Which UK tax calculator do I need?

    
Tick the situations that apply to you and the finder lists the matching calculators, most relevant first. Employees usually start with take-home pay, Scottish residents with the Scottish income tax calculator, landlords with Section 24 and Capital Gains Tax, contractors with IR35, and directors with sole trader vs limited company and dividend tax.

    
Are these calculators free?

    
Yes. Every tool is free, runs in your browser and needs no account. Support through GitHub Sponsors is optional and never changes what a tool does.

    
Is my data uploaded anywhere?

    
No. The finder only holds your ticked boxes in the page, and each calculator computes in your browser.

    
Which tax year do they cover?

    
Each tool states the year it uses on its own page, mostly 2025/26 and 2026/27. Rates change every year, so confirm figures against GOV.UK or HMRC before relying on a result.

  

  

    
No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, accounting, compliance, or financial advice. You are responsible for reviewing and verifying its output with your accountant or HMRC before relying on it.

    
Your answers. This page runs in your browser and sends nothing anywhere; closing the tab discards them, and downloads are files on your own device.

    
Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record: nothing you enter is saved anywhere.

    
Everything runs in your browser. Your answers are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (analysis_run, example_loaded, summary_downloaded) are counted only in local storage on your device, never with any of your data, and are switched off by Do Not Track.

    

    
Free and open source. If this helped, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.
